question: Can the iterative optimization of a single-pass generator itself evolve its pushforward distribution toward the data distribution, using an equilibrium-seeking sample drift at training time instead of an SDE/ODE trajectory or adversarial discriminator at inference time?

key_findings.claim: Drifting Models move iterative distribution evolution from inference into neural-network optimization by training a one-pass generator toward a stop-gradient, drifted version of its own output.
key_findings.evidence: A generator f_theta maps noise epsilon to x and induces q_theta=f_theta#p_epsilon. At training iteration i, changing theta implicitly moves the same-noise sample from f_i(epsilon) to f_{i+1}(epsilon). The paper defines a field V_{p,q}(x), sets the fixed-point target to x+V(x), and minimizes squared error between f_theta(epsilon) and stopgrad(f_theta(epsilon)+V(f_theta(epsilon))). The numerical loss equals the squared drift norm, while gradients do not backpropagate through V or q.

anchors.section: C.2 Gradients of Drifting Loss / Equations 34-36

key_findings.claim: The concrete field is a normalized mean-shift attraction to data minus repulsion from generated samples, evaluated through paired positive-negative kernels.
key_findings.evidence: For a query x, V_p^+ is a kernel-weighted mean of y^+-x for y^+ from data and V_q^- is the corresponding mean over generated y^-. Their difference can be written as an expectation of normalized k(x,y^+)k(x,y^-)(y^+-y^-). The implementation uses exponential negative Euclidean distance, row and column softmax normalization, excludes a generated point's self-distance, and estimates the field from large same-class mini-batches.

anchors.section: A.1 Pseudo-code for Computing Drifting Field V / Algorithm 2

key_findings.claim: Anti-symmetry guarantees that a matched distribution is stationary, but the paper does not prove that zero drift uniquely identifies the data distribution or that training converges to it.
key_findings.evidence: V_{p,q}=-V_{q,p} immediately gives p=q implies V=0. The converse is explicitly false for arbitrary fields and remains an open question for the implemented field. Appendix C.1 offers a heuristic under full-support smoothing, a finite-dimensional density basis, sufficiently many probes, continuity of basis approximation, and generic linear independence of all induced interaction vectors. It provides neither a general theorem for image distributions nor approximation-error or optimization-convergence bounds.

anchors.section: C.1 On Identifiability of the Zero-Drift Equilibrium

key_findings.claim: The anti-symmetric balance is empirically necessary in the paper's ImageNet ablation, but that experiment validates one design point rather than the global equilibrium theory.
key_findings.evidence: On the B/2 latent ablation after 100 epochs, the balanced V^+-V^- field obtains FID 8.46. Multiplying attraction by 1.5 or repulsion by 1.5 degrades FID to 41.05 or 46.28; factor 2 gives 86.16 or 112.84; attraction alone gives 177.14. These destructive changes alter both equilibrium and update magnitude, so they show that balance matters but do not establish that every anti-symmetric field is consistent or convergent.

key_findings.claim: High-quality ImageNet training depends critically on a separately pretrained representation space, not only on the drifting equation.
key_findings.evidence: The authors report that ImageNet training did not work without a feature encoder. At 100 generator epochs, SimCLR and MoCo features give FID 11.05 and 8.41; the custom latent-MAE improves from 8.46 at width 256/192 pretraining epochs to 4.28 at width 640/1280 epochs and 3.36 after classification fine-tuning. The final latent and pixel models use a ResNet-style MAE, and pixel models additionally use ConvNeXt-V2 features. Multi-scale, multi-location statistics and multiple temperatures are summed into many loss terms.

anchors.section: A.5 Multi-scale Features for Drifting Loss

key_findings.claim: The best latent-space model reports a new one-step ImageNet-256 FID frontier, with a quality-versus-diversity tradeoff visible in the accompanying IS.
key_findings.evidence: After scaling training from the 100-epoch B/2 ablation to 1280 epochs and then a 463M-parameter L/2 generator, the paper reports 1-NFE FID 1.54 and IS 258.9 using an SD-VAE decoder. The B/2 model obtains FID 1.75 and IS 263.2. The table's closest one-step from-scratch comparator, improved MeanFlow, has FID 1.72 and higher IS 282.0, while multi-step latent models reach lower FID such as 1.13. At matched high IS in the appendix, Drifting uses CFG 1.5 and reports FID 3.01/IS 354.4 versus the cited iMF visualization's 3.92/348.2.

key_findings.claim: The one-step pixel-space generator matches the reported FID of a strong multi-step pixel diffusion model while avoiding a VAE at inference.
key_findings.evidence: The B/16 and L/16 generators report FID 1.76/IS 299.7 and FID 1.61/IS 307.5 with one network evaluation. The table lists PixelDiT at the same 1.61 FID but 200 times 2 evaluations, and StyleGAN-XL at 2.30 FID with much higher reported FLOPs. The pixel result requires 640 generator epochs plus pixel-MAE and ConvNeXt-V2 feature encoders during training; the authors state they did not extend it to the latent model's 1280 epochs because of limited time.

anchors.section: B.1 Ablations on Pixel-Space Generation / Tables 9-10

key_findings.claim: The robotics experiment shows broadly competitive one-step control, but it does not uniformly match or exceed 100-step Diffusion Policy as the prose claims.
key_findings.evidence: Drifting improves or ties Lift, Can, BlockPush phases, and early Kitchen phases, but is lower on ToolHang visual (0.67 versus 0.73), PushT state (0.86 versus 0.91), and Kitchen phases 3-4 (0.99/0.96 versus 1.00/0.99); PushT visual is slightly higher (0.86 versus 0.84). Success is averaged over the last ten checkpoints, with no seed uncertainty or compute-matched training comparison. The evidence supports similar aggregate performance with 1 versus 100 NFE, not pointwise dominance.

key_findings.claim: One-step refers only to generator inference; the training recipe is multi-stage and computationally heavy.
key_findings.evidence: The final latent model uses a feature encoder pretrained for 1280 MAE epochs and classification-finetuned for 3,000 steps, then trains the generator for 200,000 steps/1280 epochs with effective generated batch 8192, 128 class labels, 64-128 positives per class, multiple pairwise-distance softmaxes, multi-scale losses, and VAE decoding for pixel-space feature extraction where applicable. System tables omit the training-only feature encoder from generator-plus-decoder inference parameters. Thus 'trained from scratch, not distilled' means no pretrained generative teacher, not a single-stage or representation-free training pipeline.

anchors.section: A.8 Sample Queue and A.9 Training Loop

key_findings.claim: The classifier-free-guidance equilibrium is an extrapolated signed measure for alpha greater than one and need not be a realizable probability distribution.
key_findings.evidence: Mixing unconditional real data into the negative distribution yields the stated target q_theta(.|c)=alpha p_data(.|c)-(alpha-1)p_data(.|empty) for alpha>=1. The right side can be negative on parts of the sample space, while q_theta must be nonnegative and normalized. Therefore exact equality may be impossible; training implements a weighted finite-sample field conditioned on alpha rather than minimizing a divergence to a guaranteed distribution. The headline L/2 FID happens at alpha=1, where this signed-target issue disappears.

key_findings.claim: The drifting formulation is a flexible normalized-kernel reframing of mechanisms related to MMD, mean shift, and contrastive learning rather than a wholly disconnected distribution-matching principle.
key_findings.evidence: The main text derives attraction and repulsion from mean shift and notes InfoNCE-like softmax normalization. Appendix C.2 derives the sample-movement field induced by an MMD loss and shows that a radial-kernel special case has the same attraction-minus-repulsion form. The authors distinguish their V-centric formulation by normalized kernels, explicit drift normalization/step size, and CFG, and report that their attempted MMD baseline did not work, but no quantitative MMD result is supplied.

anchors.section: 2 Related Work / Moment Matching and Contrastive Learning
C.2 The Drifting Field of MMD

key_findings.claim: Decreasing the detached drift loss is not shown to monotonically decrease a distribution discrepancy.
key_findings.evidence: Although the scalar loss value equals ||V||^2, V depends on q_theta and is explicitly detached because differentiating through the distribution is called non-trivial. Optimization therefore follows a sequence of frozen regression targets, not the full gradient of ||V_{p,q_theta}||^2. With no Lyapunov function, uniqueness theorem, or contraction condition, empirical decreasing loss and the two-dimensional toy trajectories cannot rule out cycles, spurious zeros, or finite-batch equilibria in high dimensions.

method.core_idea: Represent a generator's training trajectory as evolution of its pushforward distribution and supply each generated sample with an attraction-minus-repulsion drift whose matched-distribution equilibrium becomes a detached regression target for ordinary optimizer updates.
method.mechanism: A DiT-like one-pass network maps Gaussian and discrete style noise plus class/CFG conditions to pixels or SD-VAE latents. For each generated query, the method computes normalized exponential-distance kernels to same-class real positives and generated plus unconditional-real negatives in many pretrained feature spaces, forms a weighted positive-minus-negative drift, normalizes and sums drifts across temperatures/features, and minimizes MSE to stopgrad(feature+drift). Large-batch SGD evolves f and hence q=f#p_noise; the feature encoders are training-only.
assumptions: The selected anti-symmetric field has no practically important zero-drift equilibria other than p=q, although anti-symmetry alone proves only the forward implication.
Detached fixed-point regression follows the intended distribution evolution even though it is not the full gradient of a known discrepancy or Lyapunov objective.
A finite generated/positive batch and sample queue accurately estimate the population field and do not introduce persistent self- or batch-dependent equilibria.
Distances in pretrained MAE, MoCo, SimCLR, or ConvNeXt-V2 features preserve all perceptually and distributionally relevant distinctions needed for generation.
Matching multiple extracted feature distributions is sufficiently identifying for the pixel or latent data distribution.
Kernel temperature, feature/drift normalization, and row/column softmax avoid both flat far-distance kernels and overly local unstable interactions.
The class-conditional CFG extrapolation is useful even when its formal target alpha p_c-(alpha-1)p_uncond is not a nonnegative density.
FID and IS on 50,000 samples adequately summarize fidelity, coverage, and memorization, and published comparator values are protocol-compatible.
One-step inference efficiency can be evaluated separately from the cost of feature pretraining, large-batch pairwise kernels, long generator training, and model selection.
The ImageNet-optimized representation and architecture conclusions transfer to continuous robot-action generation, where the raw representation is used instead of a feature encoder.

techniques.role: Treats successive optimizer iterates as a sequence of generator-induced distributions rather than discretizing a trajectory at inference.
Makes p=q a stationary point by requiring that exchanging real and generated distributions flips the field sign.
Builds the drift from real-positive attraction minus generated-negative repulsion with paired kernels.
Turns a distribution-dependent sample update into an ordinary MSE target without differentiating through q.
Computes independent kernel drifts over spatial, pooled-mean, pooled-variance, and multi-resolution encoder features.
Normalizes distances and drift magnitude per feature and aggregates three temperatures to stabilize heterogeneous loss terms.
Uses weighted unconditional real negatives and conditions the generator on guidance strength while retaining one-pass inference.
Provides class-matched positives and unconditional negatives without a specialized data loader.
Uses the same drifting objective for SD-VAE-latent and direct-pixel DiT-like generators.
Replaces the iterative action generator in Diffusion Policy with the same one-pass distribution-learning principle.

evaluations.setting: Two-dimensional bimodal targets under three generated-distribution initializations, including one collapsed onto a single mode.
evaluations.metric: Visual distribution alignment and log squared-drift loss across training iterations.
evaluations.result: All shown runs approach both target modes while loss falls, including the collapsed initialization; no multi-seed quantitative divergence or failure rate is reported.
evaluations.baseline: Different adverse initializations rather than another generative method.

evaluations.setting: ImageNet-256 latent B/2 model trained 100 epochs with balanced or deliberately imbalanced attraction/repulsion.
evaluations.result: Balanced anti-symmetric V^+-V^- gives 8.46; 1.5x attraction/repulsion gives 41.05/46.28; 2x gives 86.16/112.84; attraction-only gives 177.14.

evaluations.setting: B/2, 100 epochs, effective generated batch 4096 while varying positive or negative samples per class.
evaluations.result: At 64 negatives, increasing positives 1 to 64 improves FID 20.43 to 8.46; under fixed effective batch, increasing negatives 8 to 64 improves FID 11.82 to 8.46.

evaluations.setting: B/2, 100 generator epochs, with public pixel-space SSL encoders or custom latent-MAE encoders for the drifting loss.
evaluations.result: SimCLR 11.05, MoCo-v2 8.41, latent-MAE width 256/192 epochs 8.46, width 640/1280 epochs 4.28, and the latter plus classification fine-tuning 3.36; training without a feature encoder is reported not to work.
evaluations.baseline: Alternative pretrained feature spaces and an unsuccessful raw-space attempt.

evaluations.setting: Latent-space ImageNet-256 system comparison, class conditional, 50,000 samples.
evaluations.metric: FID, IS, model parameters, and neural function evaluations.
evaluations.result: Drifting B/2: 1.75 FID/263.2 IS with 133M+49M parameters and 1 NFE; L/2: 1.54/258.9 with 463M+49M and 1 NFE. The cited iMeanFlow result is 1.72/282.0 at 1 NFE; cited multi-step results reach as low as 1.13 FID.
evaluations.baseline: Multi-step diffusion/flow models and single-step iCT, Shortcut, MeanFlow, Adversarial Flow, and improved MeanFlow.

evaluations.setting: Direct pixel-space ImageNet-256 generation without a VAE.
evaluations.metric: FID, IS, parameters, NFE, and cited generator FLOPs.
evaluations.result: B/16 obtains 1.76 FID/299.7 IS with 134M parameters; L/16 obtains 1.61/307.5 with 464M, both at 1 NFE. The paper cites 87G FLOPs for its 1.61 model versus StyleGAN-XL's 1574G and 2.30 FID.
evaluations.baseline: Multi-step pixel diffusion, EPG consistency, BigGAN, GigaGAN, and StyleGAN-XL.

evaluations.setting: Diffusion Policy protocol on Lift, Can, ToolHang, PushT, BlockPush, and Kitchen with state or visual observations as applicable.
evaluations.metric: Success rate averaged over the last ten checkpoints and inference NFE.
evaluations.result: One-step Drifting is close overall to 100-NFE Diffusion Policy and improves several entries, but loses on ToolHang visual (0.67 vs 0.73), PushT state (0.86 vs 0.91), and late Kitchen phases (0.99/0.96 vs 1.00/0.99).
evaluations.baseline: Published/reproduced 100-step Diffusion Policy under the stated common protocol.

evaluations.setting: Kernel and feature construction ablations on the 100-epoch latent B/2 default.
evaluations.result: Row-and-column kernel softmax gives 8.46, y-only softmax 8.92, and no normalization 10.54; enriching multi-scale features improves 9.58 to 9.10 to 8.46; three temperatures give 8.46 versus best single-temperature 8.67.
evaluations.baseline: Simpler normalization, feature, and temperature variants.

evaluations.setting: CLIP nearest-neighbor retrieval from the ImageNet training set plus uncurated class-conditional sample grids and a side-by-side iMeanFlow visualization.
evaluations.metric: Qualitative visual distinctness and matched-IS FID/IS operating point.
evaluations.result: Displayed generated samples are visually distinct from the ten retrieved neighbors. At CFG 1.5, Drifting reports 3.01 FID/354.4 IS versus the cited iMF visualization's 3.92/348.2; this is not a formal memorization or human-preference test.
evaluations.baseline: Retrieved training images and iMeanFlow samples for the same selected classes.

limitations: Author-stated: p=q implies V=0, but V=0 implying p=q is not generally true; conditions under which the implemented field is identifying remain unresolved.
Author-stated: the drifting field, kernels, feature encoder, and generator architecture are design choices that may be suboptimal.
Author-stated: ImageNet training could not be made to work without a feature encoder, leaving raw high-dimensional distribution matching unsolved.

Reviewer-identified: Appendix C.1 is a heuristic conditional on full support, finite basis expansions, enough probes, continuity, and generic linear independence; it supplies no nonasymptotic identifiability or convergence theorem for neural image generators.
Reviewer-identified: stop-gradient removes the q-dependent derivative of V, so the optimized update is not shown to be gradient descent on squared drift or any proper distribution divergence.

Reviewer-identified: the final system relies on a separately pretrained and classification-finetuned feature model, long generator training, huge effective batches, pairwise distances, and many feature losses; one NFE measures inference only.

Reviewer-identified: system parameter tables exclude training-only feature encoders and compare published FID/IS values without equalizing total pretraining data, training FLOPs, augmentations, hyperparameter searches, or evaluation code.
Reviewer-identified: FID and IS do not fully measure recall, mode coverage, semantic correctness, memorization, or human preference; the nearest-neighbor audit is a small qualitative CLIP retrieval.
Reviewer-identified: the formal CFG target can be a signed measure for alpha>1, so its claimed distribution-matching interpretation is not literally realizable in general.
Reviewer-identified: the sample queue is admitted to be less principled than a specialized data loader and can correlate finite-batch field estimates across updates.

Reviewer-identified: ImageNet experiments are class-conditional at one resolution, and robotics covers six established tasks; there is no unconditional large-scale image, text-to-image, video, audio, 3D, or broad control evaluation.

Reviewer-identified: robotics reports last-ten-checkpoint averages without seeds, dispersion, training compute, or statistical tests, and several subtasks are worse than Diffusion Policy despite a prose claim of matching or exceeding it.
Reviewer-identified: the MMD comparison is analytical and the paper only says its MMD attempt failed; no specified implementation or quantitative baseline supports the claimed practical advantage.

Reviewer-identified: longer training, hyperparameter changes, feature-encoder upgrades, larger generator size, and CFG operating point are changed together on the path from ablation to the headline, limiting causal attribution.
failure_modes: The field can vanish because positive and negative interactions cancel even when q differs from p, producing a spurious stationary generator.

When generated and real features are all far apart, the exponential kernel becomes nearly flat or vanishing and supplies too little directional signal; the paper observes this without a strong feature encoder.
A feature encoder can ignore texture, rare modes, spatial relations, or other distinctions, allowing feature-distribution agreement while pixel distributions remain mismatched.
Finite batches and queues can make a generated sample repel only the modes currently represented, encouraging oscillation, local collapse, or batch-specific equilibrium.
A collapsed q may not be rescued if missing modes are too distant in the learned feature metric to exert attraction, despite success in the two-dimensional toy example.
Row/column softmax and drift normalization can amplify noisy nearest neighbors or erase meaningful density magnitude, especially for rare classes.
The signed CFG target may be unattainable for large alpha, forcing an uncontrolled compromise and worsening FID beyond the operating-point sweet spot.
A feature encoder trained and tuned on ImageNet labels can make FID on the same dataset look strong without transferring to another domain or preserving within-class diversity.
Large pairwise-kernel batches and 1280-epoch training may make the method impractical where the one-step inference benefit does not amortize training cost.
Raw-action-space drift can be poorly scaled or semantically invalid in higher-dimensional, multimodal, constrained, or contact-rich control policies.
The detached target can move faster than the generator follows, creating instability because no contraction or step-size guarantee constrains successive q-dependent targets.
Published FID improvements can reverse under another evaluator, autoencoder reconstruction distribution, data preprocessing, or precision because the margins over close competitors are small.
reusable_insights: Separate an equilibrium condition, identifiability of that equilibrium, and convergence of the optimizer; p=q implies zero update proves only the first.
A distribution-dependent target can be trained through stop-gradient, but its detached vector field should be accompanied by a Lyapunov, contraction, or cycling audit.
Attraction and repulsion should be balanced so matched positive and negative distributions cancel exactly; destructive imbalance ablations are a useful diagnostic.
For kernel distribution learning in high-dimensional data, audit the feature metric as a first-class learned component and report results with raw, generic, and domain-tuned representations.
Count training-only encoders, their pretraining, pairwise-kernel cost, and total optimization steps separately from inference NFE and deployed generator parameters.
Use multiple kernel temperatures and dimension/magnitude normalization when aggregating heterogeneous feature maps, but ablate whether normalization hides density information.
Report matched-FID and matched-IS operating points because a single best FID can obscure a fidelity-coverage tradeoff.
For policy acceleration, publish every task/observation cell rather than an aggregate claim; a one-step model can be compelling even when it is slightly worse on several cells.
When guidance algebra yields a signed extrapolation, distinguish the useful heuristic field from a literal probability-distribution target.
Nearest-neighbor grids are only a preliminary memorization check; pair them with train/test nearest-neighbor statistics, precision-recall, duplicate detection, and membership inference.
open_questions: Under what verifiable conditions on the normalized kernel, feature map, and distribution family does V=0 imply p=q?
Can the detached training dynamics be shown to decrease an integral probability metric or avoid cycles and non-matching fixed points?
How sensitive are final FID, recall, and convergence to feature-encoder pretraining data, labels, architecture, seed, and frozen checkpoint?
Can an jointly learned feature metric avoid collapse without turning the system into adversarial minimax training?
What is the total training compute and energy relative to iMeanFlow, adversarial flow, diffusion, consistency, GAN, and moment-matching baselines under one common implementation?
Can the method work with smaller batches, streaming positives, approximate nearest neighbors, random features, or linear-time kernels?
Is there a nonnegative distributional interpretation of the training-time CFG construction for alpha>1, or should it be treated purely as a vector-field heuristic?
Does one-step drifting preserve rare modes and conditional diversity under precision-recall, density/coverage, and human evaluation rather than FID/IS alone?
Can raw-space or end-to-end learned drifting match ImageNet without a separately pretrained feature encoder?
How does the method scale to 512/1024 resolution, text conditioning, video, audio, 3D, and high-dimensional constrained robot actions?
Would a quantitative MMD, kernel Stein, energy-distance, or Wasserstein-gradient-flow baseline close the gap when given the same feature encoder and normalization budget?
Can the generator be warm-started or continually updated without reusing a stale feature metric and sample queue that bias the equilibrium?

competitive_landscape.title: Improved Mean Flows: On the Challenges of Fastforward Generative Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Improved MeanFlow trains a one-step generator from an average/instantaneous velocity identity, reformulates the target as stable velocity regression, and conditions explicitly on guidance, reporting 1.72 FID on ImageNet-256. Drifting reports 1.54 through an equilibrium field with no ODE and compares samples directly, but relies on a separately pretrained feature metric and lacks iMF's trajectory-derived target; at the headline FID it also has lower IS (258.9 versus the cited 282.0).

competitive_landscape.title: Mean Flows for One-step Generative Modeling
competitive_landscape.difference: MeanFlow derives a self-contained average-velocity identity and reaches 3.43 FID at 1 NFE without pretraining, distillation, or curriculum. Drifting abandons the SDE/ODE formulation and materially improves FID, but transfers much of its distribution geometry into a pretrained MAE feature encoder and has no analogous dynamical identity guaranteeing the correct target.

competitive_landscape.title: Inductive Moment Matching
competitive_landscape.difference: Inductive Moment Matching offers one- or few-step single-stage training and claims distribution-level convergence, reaching 1.99 ImageNet FID at eight steps and strong two-step CIFAR results. Drifting is natively one step and empirically stronger on ImageNet, but its own appendix concedes the missing converse V=0=>p=q; IMM therefore supplies the kind of consistency guarantee that Drifting currently replaces with a generic-independence heuristic.

competitive_landscape.title: Adversarial Flow Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Adversarial Flow learns deterministic noise-to-data maps with an adversarial objective and supports native one- or multi-step generation; its current revision reports 2.38 FID for the standard 1-NFE XL setting and 1.94 with a much deeper 112-layer single-pass model. Drifting avoids a learned discriminator and reaches 1.54, but substitutes fixed pretrained feature geometry, large positive/negative kernels, and long training for adversarial optimization.

competitive_landscape.title: PixelDiT: Pixel Diffusion Transformers for Image Generation
competitive_landscape.difference: PixelDiT removes the VAE through a hierarchical pixel diffusion transformer and reports the same 1.61 ImageNet-256 FID, plus ImageNet-512 and text-to-image results, but uses iterative diffusion inference. Drifting matches the 256 result in one pass with a simpler deployed generator, while its pixel training still depends on separately pretrained MAE and ConvNeXt-V2 feature encoders and is not tested at 512 or text-to-image scale.

competitive_landscape.title: There is No VAE: End-to-End Pixel-Space Generative Modeling via Self-Supervised Pre-training
competitive_landscape.difference: EPG likewise uses self-supervised pretraining to make pixel-space generation practical, then fine-tunes an end-to-end diffusion or consistency model; it reports 1.58 FID at 75 NFE and 8.82 for one-step consistency. Drifting's 1.61 at one NFE is the stronger speed-quality point, but both methods qualify the notion of training from scratch by relying on a substantial representation-pretraining stage.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: Drifting Models are a new generative-modeling paradigm that evolves a pushforward distribution during training through a drifting field, avoids diffusion/flow differential equations and adversarial optimization, naturally supports one-step inference, and sets new one-step ImageNet-256 FID records in latent and pixel space.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The paper defines the training-time pushforward sequence, anti-symmetric equilibrium field, detached fixed-point objective, normalized mean-shift kernel, multi-feature implementation, and training-time CFG; reports destructive anti-symmetry and representation ablations; obtains 1.54 latent and 1.61 pixel FID at one NFE; and replaces 100-NFE Diffusion Policy with broadly competitive one-step control.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The contribution is a coherent and empirically powerful V-centric synthesis of training-time pushforward evolution, mean-shift attraction/repulsion, contrastive normalization, and detached target regression. It is meaningfully distinct from trajectory regression and adversarial training, but the appendix itself connects a special case to MMD, so the foundational novelty is a flexible formulation and implementation rather than a new guarantee of distribution matching. The headline quality is compelling for inference, while claims of a complete new paradigm should remain conditional on a costly pretrained feature metric and on the unresolved gaps between matched distribution, zero drift, and optimizer convergence.
